implementation_notes: Kotlin's generator is the Sequence: a lazy, single-use sequence of values that computes each element on demand. Build one with the sequence { } builder that calls yield(...) (it suspends between elements without blocking a thread), with generateSequence(seed, nextFunction) for state-driven series, or by wrapping an Iterable with asSequence(); map/filter/takeWhile stay lazy and only a terminal operation (toList, forEach, first, sum) runs the pipeline. Prefer sequences over eagerly built lists whenever the chain is longer than the data - and use Flow (variant) when production is asynchronous.
pitfalls: Sequences are single-use and re-run the whole chain per terminal operation, so a sequence built from a mutable source can recompute side effects or throw IllegalStateException when constrained once; materialise or rebuild instead of storing a sequence for reuse.

The sequence { } builder runs on the caller's thread and yield is a suspension point, not a thread hand-off: blocking work inside the builder blocks the consumer, and mixing it with coroutine code needs Flow rather than sequences.
Operators are lazy only up to the terminal operation: sortedBy, groupBy, toList and friends materialise everything, so an infinite sequence must be bounded with take before them.

variants.name: Flow (cold asynchronous stream)
variants.idiom_name: flow { emit(x) } with suspending collectors, cancellation and flowOn
variants.implementation_notes: Flow is the asynchronous, context-preserving counterpart of Sequence: flow { } emits values from suspending code, collectors use collect and the terminal operators, backpressure is expressed by suspension rather than blocking, and cancellation propagates from the collector into the producer. It is cold - the builder runs once per collector - and flowOn moves production onto a different dispatcher. Choose Flow when elements depend on I/O, need cancellation, or must cross coroutine contexts; Sequence is cheaper when everything is CPU-local.
pitfalls: Flow is cold but not replayable: every collector restarts the producer, so sharing one stateful source across collectors needs shareIn/stateIn within a scope, and a cursor consumed by the first collector is empty for the second.

Do not emit from a nested collector: collecting another flow inside the builder runs it outside the current scope's structure (and breaks flowOn semantics); use flatMapConcat/flatMapMerge for nested streams.
